topics.label: Introduction to the complement lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture by introducing complement's importance and the challenge of its nomenclature.

topics.label: Complement fundamentals and the central role of C3
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the conceptual and molecular framework for understanding complement as a cascade centred on C3 activation.

topics.label: Complement activation pathways and the local trigger threshold
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how pathogen recognition generates enough surface-bound C3b to trigger complement activity.

topics.label: Complement effector mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how activated complement produces immune responses that eliminate pathogens.

topics.label: Complement regulation and host-cell protection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how regulatory proteins restrain complement activity to protect host cells from damage.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic connects deficiencies in particular complement components to their distinct clinical manifestations.

topics.label: Pathogen complement evasion and protein A applications
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains pathogen adaptations that evade complement, following staphylococcal protein A through to applications that exploit its antibody-binding activity.

topics.label: Lecture close and transition to adaptive immunity
topics.groupedBecause: This closing ends the complement lecture and identifies adaptive immunity as the subject of the next lecture.
